title: Zero-arc clusters merged before the embedding: stop carving and dragging arcs the contraction throws away (botijo embeds 6932 arcs, keeps 946, pays 761700 edge splits)
description:
Experiment, agreed with the user 2026-09-26. The user has tried several fixes for the contraction's edge-split explosion and none really worked; this ticket tries the idea they proposed: remove the nodes that have nothing but zero-length arcs around them before the embedding, since those nodes carry no information the layout keeps. Singular nodes are never removed.

THE PROBLEM, MEASURED. The pipeline carves every T-mesh arc into the working copy, then the contraction (LCBK19 Section 6.1: zero-arc collapse, zero-patch split and collapse) drags most of them away again, splitting an edge each time a re-route is blocked. The paper expects a blocked route to cost a few splits; ours cost thousands, because when a chain of zero arcs collapses into one node each newly dragged arc is routed between the arcs dragged before it and pays for every lane they occupy, so splits grow geometrically along the chain. Minimising splits per route (ArcRerouter already returns a fewest-split route) cannot fix that: each route is already as cheap as it can be given where the earlier arcs sit.

Sweep of master at the default curvature bias (-1), one quad-layout scene, 10 s per model; splits = working-copy vertices when the recarve starts minus when the contraction starts (one vertex per split edge); worst = largest single route at the last 500-collapse progress line.

| model | arcs embedded | arcs after contraction | splits | worst route | contract | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bolt | 334 | 84 | 921 | 2 | 0.18 s | 2.3 s |
| hand | 3547 | 1360 | 23186 | 455 | 0.55 s | 2.7 s |
| fertility | 3602 | 508 | 57011 | 2490 | 0.81 s | 4.1 s |
| rockerarm | 1572 | 402 | 37420 | 1860 | 0.93 s | 7.1 s |
| elk | 5546 | 1056 | 223171 | 12339 | 3.16 s | 7.8 s |
| botijo | 6932 | 946 | 761700 | 169851 | 4.70 s | 8.8 s |
| block, buddha, fandisk, feline | over 10 s | | | | | |

Botijo embeds 6932 arcs, keeps 946, and pays 761700 splits to throw the other 86% away. A rewrite of the collapse as plain Dijkstra in the PATCH-111 worktree gave the same numbers within a few percent (botijo 696628), so the explosion is not in the rerouter; it is in embedding and dragging arcs that do not survive.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS. After quantization, LayoutExtraction (Lyon 2021 Section 6) unions the two end nodes of every zero-quantized arc, and QuantizedMeshGrid keeps the result as `layout`. On block that gives `[layout] clusters=154 singularClusters=48 skeletonArcs=1129`, and the recarve after the full contraction ends with exactly 154 nodes. So the final node set is known before the embedding. Two things the unions do not give: the final arcs (block's 1129 skeleton arcs become 316 once the zero-patch operators merge parallel arcs), and the embedding of the survivors (the route of each arc on the surface and the cyclic order in which arcs meet a node), which is what the contraction currently works out and what the splits pay for. Quantization's validity constraints keep singularities apart (the PATCH-117 separation loop), so a zero cluster holds at most one singularity.

THE EXPERIMENT.
1. Start with the user's version: before the embedding, remove every non-singular node whose incident arcs are all zero-quantized, merging it into a neighbour, so neither it nor its zero arcs are ever carved. Measure.
2. If that helps but chains remain, go to the full version: merge each zero cluster into one node before carving, keeping the singularity when the cluster has one. Each surviving positive arc keeps its own motorcycle trace as its route; only the short connection from the trace's end to the kept node is routed, inside the cluster's region. Splits then scale with a cluster's size, not with the length of a collapse chain.
3. The paper's operators still run afterwards for whatever the pre-merge leaves: zero-area patches and any zero arc the merge could not remove.
Base this on master. PATCH-111 (the plain-Dijkstra rewrite of the collapse) is not landing and is handled separately; do not build on its worktree.

RELATED. PATCH-118 (block at bias -1: arc 178's re-carved path folds back through a vertex fan and encloses a 3-face region) may disappear if arcs are no longer dragged along collapse chains; report block's outcome either way. PATCH-117 (the quantization separation loop that keeps singularities apart). LCBK19 Section 6.1 and Def 6.2 for the operators and which endpoint may move.

UPDATE 2026-09-26: PATCH-111 (the plain-Dijkstra rewrite of the zero-arc collapse and ArcRerouter) has landed on master as 33cb78f7 after all; statements above that it is not landing are out of date. Numbers measured before it landed (the master sweep) are stale; re-baseline on current master.
definition-of-done:
1. Before the embedding, non-singular nodes whose incident arcs are all zero-quantized are removed (step 1), and, if step 1 is not enough, whole zero clusters are merged (step 2); no singular node is ever removed or moved off its vertex. The ticket records which steps were built and why.
2. Every model that loads on master at bias -1 within 10 s (bolt, hand, fertility, rockerarm, elk, botijo) still loads, with the same final '[recarve] nodes= arcs= patches=' counts as master and unchanged seamless metrics. A different count is a bug unless the ticket shows why the new layout is equally valid.
3. The ticket carries the sweep table above for the change next to master's: arcs embedded, splits, worst route, contract time, total time per model. The target is splits an order of magnitude lower on elk and botijo; if it is not reached, the ticket says what dominates the remaining splits.
4. block, buddha, fandisk and feline are run with the same 10 s cap and their outcome recorded (loaded, failed with the message, or timed out); block's outcome says whether PATCH-118's fold-back still occurs.
5. A unit test on a small hand-authored arrangement with a chain of zero arcs shows the chain merged before carving and the surviving arcs embedded without the per-chain split growth.
6. No debugging scaffolding lands (wt done's diagnostics check).
testing-plan:
1. Baseline: in one quad-layout scene on master, load bolt, hand, feline, botijo, fandisk, elk, block, fertility, rockerarm (figure_8 and figure_9) and buddha with `ixdar-cli model`, each wrapped in `timeout 10`; on overrun kill the scene's JVM, record a timeout and start a fresh scene (one log per scene). Never load sphere_random. Read splits from the first '[contract] collapses=' line's V= and the '[recarve] ... copy V=X->' line, arcs from '[embed] arcs=' and '[recarve] ... arcs='.
2. Build step 1, rerun the sweep, compare.
3. If needed build step 2, rerun, compare.
4. Unit tests (DoD 5) and the full suite.
5. Launch entry for quad-layout on botijo and a screenshot under tmp/.
unknowns: Zero-area patches: can the pre-merge also settle the zero-patch cases (operators 2 and 3), or do those stay with the embedded operators?
Cyclic order at a merged node: where several surviving arcs arrive at one kept node, what fixes the order they meet it in without dragging them one by one?

Does a cluster's region (the union of its zero arcs' neighbouring patches) always contain a split-free route from each surviving trace's end to the kept node, or does step 2 still need the rerouter's edge splits there?
changes-made: Baseline confirmed 2026-09-26: the worktree sweep before any change reproduces master's table exactly (bolt 921, hand 23186, fertility 57011, rockerarm 37420, elk 223171, botijo 761700 splits; block, buddha, fandisk, feline over 10 s). Candidates measured: non-critical nodes whose arcs are all zero are 19/179 on bolt, 72/1813 hand, 262/2841 elk, 451/2076 block, 603/3540 botijo; they touch 1661 of botijo's 4631 zero arcs.

Step 1 built as ZeroNodeMerge (embedding/): before the carve, interior nodes are unioned with zero neighbours into sets holding at most one non-interior node, refusing any union that would create a loop or a parallel pair; tree arcs are dropped from patch sides and never carved, each arc left at a merged node is re-pointed at the kept node and carved along the collapsed arcs' traces then its own. Arcs sharing a collapsed arc's trace are ordered across it by a counter-clockwise tour of the set's tree (lane keys on FaceStripPath, tie-break in SnappingCarve.grantCorners, near-equal traced positions aligned). ArcNetwork.assemble starts a patch walk at sideNodeIds when the merge filled them.

Step 1 outcome: most merges cannot be carved. Zero clusters are sub-triangle tight (nodes minted a fraction of an edge apart around one mesh vertex), so shared route pieces turn back across the same constraint edge (U-turn at a merged node) or lose shared crossings to trimEndCrossings next to a node vertex, and the laid chords then cross. Those merged nodes are detected per piece (SnappingCarve.unlayableRouteNodes), frozen and the carve redone; after 3-4 rounds only 6/16 merges survive on bolt, 9/67 hand, 21/228 elk, 52/501 botijo. Final recarve counts equal master's on bolt, hand, elk, botijo; splits unchanged within noise (botijo 815942 vs 761700, elk 220871 vs 223171).

Step 1 sweep (pre-PATCH-111 master base, bias -1, 10 s cap), model: outcome arcs-embedded/after splits worst contract gridmap. bolt loaded 328/84 1021 11 0.09s; hand loaded 3538/1360 20631 163 0.49s; botijo TIMEOUT (contract finished 5.63s, 6880/946, 815889 splits, worst 187317; loaded in 9.7 s on an earlier run); elk loaded 5525/1056 220851 12339 3.19s; fertility loaded 3565/508 49755 2490 1.24s; rockerarm fig8 timeout / fig9 loaded 9.8 s, 1560/402 27215 1352 1.27s; block timeout (embed 3992 arcs, worst 2022); feline, fandisk, buddha timeout. Recarve counts equal master wherever the recarve ran. Splits: no order-of-magnitude change (botijo +7%, elk -1%, hand -11%, fertility -13%, rockerarm -27%, bolt +11%); load times rose from the repeated slice rounds. Conclusion: step 1 as trace concatenation merges too few nodes to matter; the chains that drive splits sit in exactly the tight clusters the carve cannot lay concatenated routes through.

Synced onto master 9f5a5fce (PATCH-111 landed) with no conflicts; the step-1 diff (ZeroNodeMerge.java new; ArcNetwork, FaceStripPath, LayoutEmbedding, SnappingCarve edited) now sits on the rewritten collapse. The baseline needs a run without the step-1 diff, e.g. split_sweep.sh against the main checkout; the agent stopped at its context budget before this.
